findings.title: Chain verification does not authenticate statement or justification payloads
findings.evidence: verify_chain hashes stored s_hash/j_hash only (lines 345-374); get_statement/get_justification load payloads without recomputing hashes (497-526). publisher.rs:31-47 verifies then exports these payloads; bindings.rs:35-44 rehydrates them.
findings.trigger: Modify statements.content/modality/obligations_json or justifications.payload_json in an existing database without changing their hash keys.
findings.impact: Replay and export accept altered knowledge while chain verification succeeds; valid JSON tampering is not detected.

findings.title: Nogood primary key prevents revoking the same statement in multiple environments
findings.evidence: atms_nogoods_log declares nogood_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY rather than (nogood_hash, environment_id); assert_nogood unconditionally inserts at 335-338.
findings.trigger: Call assert_nogood(hash, env_a), then assert_nogood(hash, env_b), or repeat the same revocation.
findings.impact: Second revocation returns a SQLite uniqueness error, preventing a per-environment causal revocation record and making retry non-idempotent.

findings.title: Derived assertion and explicit dependency edges commit separately
findings.evidence: assert_derived_knowledge calls assert_knowledge, which commits at 299, before beginning its edge transaction at 312; replay propagation relies on edges at 444-465.
findings.trigger: Process stops or edge insertion/commit fails after assert_knowledge commits and before assert_derived_knowledge commits its edges.
findings.impact: A persisted derived assertion survives without its explicit causal parents, so subsequent revocation closure may omit it.

findings.title: Technical specification recommends weaker persistence than the canonical contract
findings.evidence: Connection configuration uses PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL; .babylon60rules requires synchronous = FULL and ledger.rs:57 implements FULL.
findings.trigger: An implementer copies section 3.1 as the connection configuration for a new persistent ledger.
findings.impact: The normative example contradicts the required durability setting and can propagate a weaker persistence configuration.

findings.title: Multi-tenant example trusts a caller-selected identity
findings.evidence: userId comes directly from X-User-ID; getSession(userId) and createSession({id:userId}) use it within the shared multi-tenant sandbox (170-181).
findings.trigger: Deploy the documented handler where different callers can set X-User-ID and request another caller's session ID.
findings.impact: The example supplies no authentication binding, allowing session selection across tenants if adopted directly; this is an example defect, not evidence of a deployed service.

findings.title: CI example interpolates request JSON into a shell command
findings.evidence: repo and branch are read from request.json at 135 and directly interpolated into sandbox.exec git clone at 138.
findings.trigger: Adopt the example and submit shell metacharacters through repo or branch.
findings.impact: Input changes the command structure and can execute unintended shell commands inside the CI sandbox; no host escape is claimed.

hypotheses.description: The code-execution example also interpolates arbitrary code into python3 -c shell syntax; whether a particular Cloudflare SDK version adds command-layer protections was not verified. The explicit code execution feature itself is intentional.
